summary.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27: consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 Mt volume; guides FY27 cost INR4,250/t and 149 Mt by FY29.
summary.overview: Ambuja Cements (consolidated, including ACC and Orient) reported Q2 FY27 cement volume of 16.5 Mt, revenue of INR9,197 crore, EBITDA of INR1,271 crore and PAT of INR236 crore. Trade volumes rose 8.6% YoY with trade share at 74%, while B2B volumes were still negative, so overall volume was roughly flat. Management announced 14 expansion projects adding about 30 Mt of cement and 10.3 Mt of clinker, with capex of about INR14,500 crore, and said the ACC and Orient mergers will now go to NCLT with completion targeted within FY27. Price held at INR255/bag, with INR10/bag realised in October.

segments.name: Trade (cement)
segments.commentary: Trade volume up 8.6% YoY; trade share up to 74%; premium products 37% of trade sales (35% last year). North trade +13%, Central +9%, West +14%, East flat, South +13%.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B
segments.commentary: B2B volumes still negative YoY in Q2 after management sacrificed negative-EBITDA volumes; management expects both trade and B2B to turn positive in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Blended cement
segments.commentary: Blended share of sales rose to 82% from 77%; management targets an 80:20 blended to OPC mix.

segments.name: Ancillary (RE power, fly ash, RMC)
segments.commentary: Green power sales revenue ~INR136 crore (352 million kWh) in Q2; fly ash revenue ~INR25 crore; RMC EBITDA margin ~7%. Power sales booked in other operating income.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cost target INR4,250/t retained; management cites ~INR160/t improvement in H2 and says the cost guidance is baked in.
H2 FY27 volume growth to be above industry, with management aiming for higher single digit and possibly double digit growth.
Exit FY27 capacity utilisation expected at ~75%, versus ~61-62% in Q2.
Capacity of 113.5 Mt to reach ~149 Mt by FY29 and ~155 Mt by FY30; FY28 cost target INR4,000/t on the combined capacity base.
Capex for the 30 Mt expansion ~INR14,500 crore, about INR7,500 crore a year; FY27 capex ~INR6,500-7,000 crore with ~INR3,000-3,500 crore left for H2.
Expects ~INR150/t cumulative benefit from trade-led value focus by June, with INR40/t extra per quarter.
Mergers of ACC and Orient into Ambuja to go to NCLT; completion targeted within FY27 and expected to be EPS accretive.
capex_capacity: 14 expansion projects adding ~30 Mt cement and 10.3 Mt clinker: West 15.2 Mt grinding, East 11.6 Mt, North 2.9 Mt; new clinker at Maratha (4 Mt), Umrangso (4 Mt) and Mundra (2.25 Mt).
Q2 commissioned 4.6 Mt (Dahej, Salai Banwa, Kalamboli); 3.2 Mt at Bathinda and Penna Jodhpur stabilised and ramping in H2; 2.4 Mt Warisaliganj due in H2 FY27 (Q3 per Q&A).
Build timelines of ~14 months for grinding units and ~18 months for integrated units; equipment already ordered and PMC appointed.
Penna and Sanghi utilisation ~50%; company-level utilisation ~61-62% in Q2.
Debottlenecking projects (about 4, with Loesche) to complete in 4-5 months.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt with clinker factor ~66%.
demand_pricing: Price held at INR255/bag through a weak monsoon quarter; INR10/bag realised in October with further hikes expected.
Management says it is pursuing value over volume but aims not to lose market share; brand-equity surveys cited as supporting realisation.
Industry demand expected at ~6-7% for FY27 per company presentation; H1 growth ~8% by the company's count.
Monsoon deficit and state drought declarations flagged as a lagged headwind for Q3 and Q4 construction activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why start a new capex wave now when H1 volumes were negative and demand is soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarterly performance did not drive the decision; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the second wave is described as value-accretive, largely brownfield, and clinker-backed.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed to reach 149 Mt, and how does the debt position evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR14,500 crore for 30 Mt, roughly INR7,500 crore a year; management describes the programme as self-sustaining from cash flows with only interim debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence on execution, given ~20 Mt bunched into Mar-May 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited past contractor issues, now resolved, and a tighter schedule of ~14 months for grinding units and ~18 for integrated units.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fuel cost on spot basis versus the Q2 blend?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported spot fuel is INR2.80-2.85 per 1,000 kcal, versus a Q2 blend of INR1.87; the imported share is under 40% and pet coke is ~10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,000/t cost target inclusive of new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the INR4,000/t target for FY28 covers the combined existing and new capacity, with 149 Mt in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to the merger tax shield from acquired entities such as Penna and Sanghi.

risks_watch: Capex execution risk: ~20 Mt commissioning bunched in Mar-May 2028; Chinese equipment supply chain flagged as an area for improvement.
Fuel cost inflation: spot imported fuel ~INR2.85 vs Q2 blend INR1.87; management expects fuel cost to rise, which must be offset to reach the INR4,250/t target.
Monsoon and drought in key states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra, Rajasthan) could moderate construction in Q3-Q4.
Competitive intensity in East and West grinding expansion, with peers adding similar capacity.
Institutional volumes still negative YoY; Q3 and Q4 targets require a turn to growth.
Pending NCLT approval for the ACC and Orient mergers; company expects completion within FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the expansion path and cost trajectory, but cautious on near-term demand, citing geopolitics, energy costs and weak monsoon. Evasive on the exact spot fuel and price trajectory, and on the capex reason for timing; it re-emphasised value over volume without giving hard volume targets.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 volume growth of higher single digit (possibly double digit), ahead of industry, and exit-FY27 utilisation of ~75% from ~61-62%, backed by ~4.6 Mt commissioned in Q2 and 3.2 Mt ramping plus 2.4 Mt Warisaliganj due in H2, with 30 Mt expansion (INR14,500 crore) targeting 149 Mt by FY29.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management retains INR4,250/t FY27 cost target citing ~INR160/t H2 improvement and ~INR150/t trade-led value benefit by June, though spot imported fuel at INR2.80-2.85 vs Q2 blend INR1.87 is a headwind to offset.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Q2 commissioned 4.6 Mt, 3.2 Mt at Bathinda and Penna Jodhpur ramping in H2, and 2.4 Mt Warisaliganj due in H2 FY27 (Q3 per Q&A), so new capacity is already under way with dates.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 volume growth of higher single digit (possibly double digit), ahead of industry, with trade up 8.6% YoY and B2B expected to turn positive in Q3/Q4, though utilisation is only ~61-62% and monsoon is a lagged headwind.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The 14-project, ~30 Mt, INR14,500 crore expansion was announced on this call (~INR7,500 crore a year, FY27 capex INR6,500-7,000 crore), so the new capex is already out; utilisation of ~61-62% gives no push for a further announcement near term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said price held at INR255/bag with INR10/bag realised in October and further hikes expected, and H2 volume growth is guided above industry, but demand is soft and the call stressed value over volume.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spot imported fuel at INR2.80-2.85/1,000 kcal vs Q2 blend INR1.87 and monsoon/drought in key states could hit Q3-Q4 construction, putting the INR4,250/t cost target and volume turn at risk.

rows.label: ACC and Orient mergers into Ambuja via NCLT
rows.why: Mergers go to NCLT with completion targeted within FY27 and expected to be EPS accretive, though approval is still pending.

rows.label: Institutional/B2B volumes turn positive
rows.why: B2B volumes still negative YoY in Q2 after management sacrificed negative-EBITDA volumes; management expects both trade and B2B to turn positive in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Power cost reduction from green power
rows.why: Net power cost fell to INR4.8/unit from INR6/unit a year ago, with ~352 million kWh green power sold for ~INR136 crore in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the expansion path, the INR4,250/t cost target and the H2 volume turn, but cautious on near-term demand, citing weak monsoon, geopolitics and energy costs.
